answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% component spend reduction and the incumbent has refused to reopen pricing. Historical evidence (memory_c2) proves that switching to a low-cost primary vendor achieved sharp unit cost cuts with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing, indicating manageable transition risk. Current production at 94% capacity with no buffer requires decisive action. Switching primary vendor is the most direct path to meeting the immediate cost mandate while leveraging proven supplier performance. Memory_c3 confirms that risk mitigation via dual sourcing works, but the urgent cost imperative and single-decision constraint favor a primary vendor transition to achieve required savings within the cycle.
